rationale: Mathematicians and statisticians analyze data and develop models. Entirely computational knowledge work.

title: Mechanical engineering technologists and technicians
rationale: Mechanical engineering techs build prototypes and test equipment in labs and shops. The hands-on work in semi-structured environments has moderate physical exposure, but varied tasks limit automation.

title: Mechanical engineers
rationale: Mechanical engineers design mechanical systems. Knowledge-based engineering work.

title: Medical and health services managers
rationale: Healthcare managers oversee facilities, staff, and operations. Their work is entirely managerial and administrative with no physical labor component exposed to robotic automation.

title: Medical assistants
rationale: Medical assistants perform varied clinical and administrative tasks in healthcare settings. The mix of patient interaction, clinical procedures, and administrative work in variable situations limits robotic exposure.

title: Medical dosimetrists
rationale: Medical dosimetrists calculate radiation doses using specialized software. Their work is primarily computational and knowledge-based with no physical labor component for robots to automate.

title: Medical equipment repairers
rationale: Medical equipment repair involves diagnosing and fixing diverse electronic and mechanical medical devices. The variety of equipment and clinical settings limits robotic deployment by 2028.

title: Medical records specialists
rationale: Medical records specialists organize and manage health data. This is entirely desk-based knowledge work with no physical labor component.

title: Medical scientists
rationale: Medical scientists conduct research in laboratories, which involves some physical lab work. However, their role is primarily research-focused with lab automation handling routine sample processing.

title: Medical transcriptionists
rationale: Medical transcriptionists convert voice recordings to written reports. This is purely desk-based knowledge work with no physical component for robots to automate.

title: Meeting, convention, and event planners
rationale: Event planners coordinate meetings and events. Organizational and interpersonal work.

title: Metal and plastic machine workers
rationale: Machine operation in metal and plastics manufacturing involves repetitive tasks in controlled factory settings. Robotic loading/unloading and tending of these machines is commercially deployed by 2028.

title: Microbiologists
rationale: Microbiologists conduct research in laboratories. While lab work involves some physical handling, the role is primarily research-focused knowledge work.

title: Middle school teachers
rationale: Teaching is fundamentally interpersonal and cognitive work involving instruction, mentoring, and classroom management. There is no physical labor component for robots to automate.

title: Military careers
rationale: Military careers span a huge range from combat to administrative roles. Physical tasks include equipment operation and maintenance in varied conditions. Some logistics automation is advancing, but most military physical tasks remain manual.

title: Mining and geological engineers
rationale: Mining engineers design mining operations. Knowledge-based engineering work.

title: Models
rationale: Models pose for visual media. This is a physical but creative/performative role that robots cannot meaningfully replace.

title: Music directors and composers
rationale: Music directors lead ensembles and composers create music. Creative artistic work.

title: Musicians and singers
rationale: Musicians perform music requiring artistic expression. Creative performance that robots cannot meaningfully replicate.

title: Natural sciences managers
rationale: Natural sciences managers oversee research teams. Managerial work.

title: Network and computer systems administrators
rationale: Network admins manage computer networks and systems. Desk-based technical work.

title: News analysts, reporters, and journalists
rationale: Journalists research and report news. Knowledge-based communication work.

title: Nuclear engineers
rationale: Nuclear engineers design nuclear systems. Knowledge-based engineering work.

title: Nuclear medicine technologists
rationale: Nuclear medicine techs prepare and administer radioactive drugs and operate imaging equipment. The patient interaction and safety-critical material handling limit robotic replacement by 2028.

title: Nuclear technicians
rationale: Nuclear technicians operate and monitor nuclear equipment in controlled plant environments. The structured, regulated environment has some automation potential, but safety-critical operations still require human oversight.

title: Nurse anesthetists, nurse midwives, and nurse practitioners
rationale: Advanced practice nurses perform clinical examinations, procedures, and patient care. The varied patient conditions and clinical judgment required limit robotic replacement by 2028.

title: Nursing assistants and orderlies
rationale: Nursing assistants provide direct physical care to patients including bathing, feeding, and mobility assistance. The intimate, varied patient interactions require human empathy and adaptability beyond 2028 robotics.

title: Occupational health and safety specialists and technicians
rationale: Safety specialists inspect workplaces and enforce regulations. Primarily analytical and inspection-based work with site visits but no physical labor.

title: Occupational therapists
rationale: Occupational therapists help patients develop or recover daily living skills through personalized physical activities. The highly individualized, adaptive nature of therapy limits robotic replacement by 2028.

title: Occupational therapy assistants and aides
rationale: OT assistants help patients with therapeutic activities and exercises. The personalized, adaptive physical interactions with patients are beyond 2028 robotic capabilities.

title: Oil and gas workers
rationale: Oil and gas workers operate drilling equipment in variable outdoor environments. While some automation exists for drilling, the harsh and variable conditions of oilfields limit robotic deployment by 2028.

title: Operations research analysts
rationale: Operations research analysts use mathematical models to solve problems. Entirely desk-based analytical work.

title: Opticians
rationale: Dispensing opticians fit and adjust eyeglasses for customers. The customer interaction and precise adjustment work is primarily service-oriented with minimal physical labor for robots to automate.

title: Optometrists
rationale: Optometrists examine eyes and prescribe corrective measures. The work involves clinical examination equipment but is primarily diagnostic, with minimal physical labor component for robots to automate.

title: Orthotists and prosthetists
rationale: Orthotists and prosthetists design and fit custom devices for patients. While 3D printing automates some fabrication, the patient fitting and customization require skilled manual work in variable situations.

title: Painters, construction and maintenance
rationale: Construction painters work in variable building environments with different surfaces and conditions. Unlike factory spray painting, the unstructured nature of construction sites limits robotic painting deployment by 2028.

title: Painting and coating workers
rationale: Industrial painting and coating in manufacturing is performed in controlled environments with repetitive motions. Robotic spray painting is already standard in automotive; by 2028 it extends further into general manufacturing.

title: Paralegals and legal assistants
rationale: Paralegals research legal documents and assist lawyers. Desk-based legal support work.

title: Personal financial advisors
rationale: Financial advisors provide investment and financial planning advice. Interpersonal advisory work.

title: Pest control workers
rationale: Pest control involves visiting diverse residential and commercial environments to identify and treat infestations. The variable settings and diagnostic assessment required limit robotic deployment by 2028.

title: Petroleum engineers
rationale: Petroleum engineers design extraction methods. Knowledge-based engineering work.

title: Pharmacists
rationale: Pharmacists primarily provide clinical consultation and medication management (knowledge work), but also oversee physical dispensing. Robotic dispensing handles the physical component while pharmacists focus on clinical roles.

title: Pharmacy technicians
rationale: Pharmacy technicians count, label, and dispense medications in structured pharmacy environments. Automated dispensing systems and robotic pharmacy fulfillment are commercially deployed in hospital and retail pharmacies by 2028.

title: Phlebotomists
rationale: Phlebotomists draw blood requiring precise venipuncture on varied patients. Automated blood-drawing devices are in development, but patient vein variability and the need for patient comfort limit deployment by 2028.

title: Photographers
rationale: Photographers use cameras in varied settings to capture images. While some automated photography exists (photo booths), creative photography in variable environments requires human judgment.

title: Physical therapist assistants and aides
rationale: PT assistants help patients perform exercises and provide hands-on care under therapist supervision. The varied patient needs and physical interaction requirements limit robotic exposure by 2028.

title: Physical therapists
rationale: Physical therapists guide patients through exercises and manual therapy requiring clinical judgment and physical interaction. The varied patient conditions and need for adaptive touch limit robotic replacement by 2028.

title: Physician assistants
rationale: Physician assistants examine patients and perform clinical procedures. The varied patient encounters and clinical judgment required limit physical robotic automation by 2028.

title: Physicians and surgeons
rationale: Surgeons use robotic surgical systems (da Vinci) as tools, but these augment rather than replace the surgeon. The complex judgment and varied patient situations keep physical automation exposure minimal.

title: Physicists and astronomers
rationale: Physicists conduct research using theoretical and experimental methods. Knowledge-based scientific work.

title: Plumbers, pipefitters, and steamfitters
rationale: Plumbers work in highly variable residential and commercial environments where every building presents different configurations. The unpredictable physical environment and fine manual dexterity required are beyond 2028 robotics.

title: Podiatrists
rationale: Podiatrists diagnose and treat foot conditions with clinical examination and procedures. The varied patient conditions and fine clinical manual work limit robotic replacement by 2028.

title: Police and detectives
rationale: Police work involves unpredictable physical situations, community interaction, and investigative judgment. The highly variable and socially complex nature of policing makes robotic replacement minimal by 2028.

title: Political scientists
rationale: Political scientists study political systems. Entirely knowledge-based research work.

title: Postal service workers
rationale: Postal workers sort and deliver mail, combining structured sorting facility work with unstructured delivery routes. Sorting automation is well advanced; delivery remains difficult for robots due to variable residential environments.

title: Postsecondary education administrators
rationale: Education administrators perform management, planning, and coordination. Their work is entirely administrative and cognitive with no physical labor component.

title: Postsecondary teachers
rationale: Teaching is fundamentally interpersonal and cognitive work involving instruction, mentoring, and classroom management. There is no physical labor component for robots to automate.

title: Power plant operators, distributors, and dispatchers
rationale: Power plant operators monitor and control equipment in structured plant environments. Control room operations are increasingly automated, and some physical plant maintenance tasks are in controlled environments.

title: Preschool and childcare center directors
rationale: Education administrators perform management, planning, and coordination. Their work is entirely administrative and cognitive with no physical labor component.

title: Preschool teachers
rationale: Teaching is fundamentally interpersonal and cognitive work involving instruction, mentoring, and classroom management. There is no physical labor component for robots to automate.

title: Private detectives and investigators
rationale: Private investigators conduct research, surveillance, and interviews. Their work is primarily cognitive and interpersonal with no physical labor component for robots to automate.

title: Probation officers and correctional treatment specialists
rationale: Probation officers conduct assessments and supervise offenders through meetings and evaluations. This is interpersonal and administrative work with no physical labor component.

title: Producers and directors
rationale: Producers and directors oversee film and media production. Creative and managerial work.

title: Project management specialists
rationale: Project managers plan and oversee projects. Managerial knowledge work.

title: Property appraisers and assessors
rationale: Property appraisers evaluate real estate values. Analytical work with site visits but no physical labor.

title: Property, real estate, and community association managers
rationale: Property managers oversee real estate operations. Managerial work.

title: Psychiatric technicians and aides
rationale: Psychiatric techs provide care to patients with mental illness, including physical assistance and monitoring. The interpersonal nature and unpredictable patient interactions limit robotic replacement.

title: Psychologists
rationale: Psychologists study behavior and provide therapy. Cognitive and interpersonal work.

title: Public relations and fundraising managers
rationale: PR managers oversee public communications. Strategic communication work.

title: Public relations specialists
rationale: PR specialists manage public image through communications. Knowledge-based communication work.

title: Public safety telecommunicators
rationale: Dispatchers coordinate emergency responses from communication centers. Desk-based communication work.

title: Purchasing managers, buyers, and purchasing agents
rationale: Purchasing managers negotiate and procure goods. Desk-based negotiation and analytical work.

title: Quality control inspectors
rationale: Quality inspection in manufacturing involves repetitive visual and measurement checks in structured factory environments. Machine vision and robotic inspection systems are being commercially deployed in automotive and electronics by 2028.

title: Radiation therapists
rationale: Radiation therapists position patients precisely for treatment using linear accelerators. Patient positioning is somewhat structured, and automated positioning systems are advancing, but patient variability limits full automation.

title: Radiologic and MRI technologists
rationale: Radiologic techs position patients and operate imaging equipment. Each patient requires different positioning, and the patient interaction component limits physical robotic automation by 2028.

title: Railroad workers
rationale: Railroad work includes operating trains on fixed tracks (structured, automatable) and physical tasks like coupling cars and track maintenance. Train automation is advancing on freight corridors, but physical maintenance remains manual.

title: Real estate brokers and sales agents
rationale: Real estate agents facilitate property sales through showings and negotiations. Interpersonal sales work.

title: Receptionists
rationale: Receptionists greet visitors and manage front desk communications. Communication and administrative work.

title: Recreation workers
rationale: Recreation workers plan and lead leisure activities. Interpersonal facilitation work.

title: Recreational therapists
rationale: Recreational therapists plan and lead activities for patients. While activities involve some physical demonstration, the work is primarily therapeutic facilitation with minimal robotic exposure.

title: Registered nurses
rationale: Nurses perform diverse physical care tasks for patients with varied conditions in unpredictable clinical environments. The high variability and need for empathetic human judgment make robotic replacement minimal by 2028.

title: Rehabilitation counselors
rationale: Rehabilitation counselors help people with disabilities. Interpersonal counseling work.

title: Respiratory therapists
rationale: Respiratory therapists manage ventilators and provide breathing treatments to patients with varied conditions. The clinical judgment and varied patient situations limit physical robotic exposure.

title: Retail sales workers
rationale: Retail workers stock shelves and assist customers in store environments. Large chain retailers are piloting robotic shelf stocking, but customer assistance and varied store layouts limit broader replacement by 2028.

title: Roofers
rationale: Roofing involves physically demanding work at heights on varied building structures. The unstructured, hazardous outdoor environment and varied roof configurations make robotic replacement infeasible by 2028.

title: Sales engineers
rationale: Sales engineers sell complex technical products. Technical sales and consulting work.

title: Sales managers
rationale: Sales managers oversee sales teams and strategies. Managerial work.

title: School and career counselors and advisors
rationale: School counselors advise students on academic and career paths. Interpersonal advisory work.

title: Secretaries and administrative assistants
rationale: Administrative assistants provide office support. Desk-based clerical work.

title: Securities, commodities, and financial services sales agents
rationale: Financial services sales agents sell securities and investments. Desk-based sales and analytical work.

title: Security guards and gambling surveillance officers
rationale: Security guards patrol and monitor facilities. Robotic security patrols (like Knightscope) are deployed in some structured environments like malls and campuses, but human guards are still needed for varied situations and interventions.

title: Semiconductor processing technicians
rationale: Semiconductor fabrication environments are highly controlled cleanrooms with repetitive wafer handling and processing steps. Much of the physical workflow is already automated, and robotic handling is commercially deployed at scale.

title: Set and exhibit designers
rationale: Set designers create physical spaces for productions and exhibits. While design is cognitive, construction involves physical work in variable settings, limiting robotic exposure.

title: Sheet metal workers
rationale: Sheet metal work spans factory fabrication (more structured) and field installation (variable). Factory-based sheet metal cutting and forming is increasingly automated, but field installation remains manual by 2028.

title: Skincare specialists
rationale: Skincare specialists perform facial treatments and skin analysis on varied clients. The intimate client contact and varied skin conditions require adaptive human touch beyond 2028 robotics.

title: Small engine mechanics
rationale: Small engine repair involves diagnosing and fixing varied equipment in workshop settings. While more structured than field work, the variety of equipment and repairs limits robotic deployment by 2028.

title: Social and community service managers
rationale: Social service managers oversee community programs. Managerial and interpersonal work.

title: Social and human service assistants
rationale: Social service assistants help clients access services. Interpersonal support work.

title: Social workers
rationale: Social workers help people cope with challenges. Interpersonal therapeutic and advocacy work.

title: Sociologists
rationale: Sociologists study social behavior. Knowledge-based research work.

title: Software developers, quality assurance analysts, and testers
rationale: Software developers design and write code. Entirely desk-based knowledge work.

title: Solar photovoltaic installers
rationale: Solar panel installation involves physical labor on varied rooftops and ground-mount structures. While large utility-scale installations have some automation potential, residential and varied commercial sites limit robotic deployment by 2028.

title: Special education teachers
rationale: Teaching is fundamentally interpersonal and cognitive work involving instruction, mentoring, and classroom management. There is no physical labor component for robots to automate.

title: Special effects artists and animators
rationale: Animators and special effects artists create digital visual content. Desk-based creative technical work.

title: Speech-language pathologists
rationale: Speech-language pathologists provide therapy through communication and exercises. Their work is primarily cognitive and interpersonal with no significant physical labor component for robots to automate.

title: Stationary engineers and boiler operators
rationale: Stationary engineers operate and maintain boilers and mechanical systems in buildings and plants. While monitoring is increasingly automated, the physical maintenance and repair work requires skilled judgment in variable conditions.

title: Substance abuse, behavioral disorder, and mental health counselors
rationale: Mental health counselors provide therapy and support. Interpersonal therapeutic work.

title: Surgical assistants and technologists
rationale: Surgical technologists prepare operating rooms and assist during procedures in structured but high-stakes environments. While robotic surgery systems are deployed, the technologist's varied support role remains manual.

title: Survey researchers
rationale: Survey researchers design and conduct surveys. Knowledge-based research work.

title: Surveying and mapping technicians
rationale: Survey techs collect data using field equipment. Some fieldwork with physical equipment, but GPS and drone technology already assist. Variable outdoor conditions limit full robotic exposure.

title: Surveyors
rationale: Surveyors measure land using specialized equipment in variable outdoor settings. Drone surveying is advancing, but ground-level work in varied terrain limits full robotic replacement.

title: Tax examiners and collectors, and revenue agents
rationale: Tax examiners review tax returns and collect revenue. Desk-based analytical and administrative work.

title: Taxi drivers, shuttle drivers, and chauffeurs
rationale: Autonomous ride-hailing (Waymo, Zoox) is commercially operational in 15-20 US cities by 2028 on geo-fenced routes, directly displacing taxi/chauffeur functions in those markets. Significant but not universal coverage.

title: Teacher assistants
rationale: Teaching assistance and tutoring involve interpersonal instruction and student support. This is cognitive and social work with no physical labor component for robots to automate.

title: Technical writers
rationale: Technical writers create documentation. Desk-based knowledge work.

title: Telecommunications technicians
rationale: Telecom technicians install and repair equipment in varied residential and commercial buildings. The diverse environments and need for diagnostic troubleshooting limit robotic deployment by 2028.

title: Tellers
rationale: Bank tellers process transactions at counters. ATMs and digital banking have already automated much of this work; remaining teller work involves customer interaction, not physical labor.

title: Top executives
rationale: Top executives make strategic business decisions. Entirely leadership and knowledge work.

title: Tour and travel guides
rationale: Tour guides lead groups and provide commentary. Interpersonal communication work.

title: Training and development managers
rationale: Training managers oversee employee development programs. Managerial work.

title: Training and development specialists
rationale: Training specialists design and deliver training programs. Knowledge-based educational work.

title: Transportation, storage, and distribution managers
rationale: Distribution managers oversee logistics operations. Managerial work.

title: Travel agents
rationale: Travel agents plan trips for clients. Service-oriented desk work.

title: Tutors
rationale: Teaching assistance and tutoring involve interpersonal instruction and student support. This is cognitive and social work with no physical labor component for robots to automate.

title: Umpires, referees, and other sports officials
rationale: Sports officials enforce rules during competitions. While technology assists with some calls, officiating requires human judgment in dynamic environments.

title: Urban and regional planners
rationale: Urban planners develop land use plans. Knowledge-based analytical and design work.

title: Veterinarians
rationale: Veterinarians perform examinations and procedures on diverse animal species in unpredictable clinical settings. The variability of animal patients and procedures limits robotic replacement by 2028.

title: Veterinary assistants and laboratory animal caretakers
rationale: Vet assistants and lab animal caretakers feed, clean, and handle animals in somewhat structured settings. Lab animal care is more structured than clinical vet work, but animal handling limits automation.

title: Veterinary technologists and technicians
rationale: Vet techs assist with animal procedures requiring handling of unpredictable animals. The variable animal behavior and diverse clinical tasks limit robotic exposure by 2028.

title: Waiters and waitresses
rationale: Waiters navigate variable dining environments while carrying food and interacting with customers. Some restaurants use delivery robots, but the social interaction and varied environments limit robotic replacement by 2028.

title: Water and wastewater treatment plant and system operators
rationale: Water treatment operators monitor and adjust equipment in structured plant environments. Plant operations are increasingly automated with SCADA systems, and some physical monitoring tasks have robotic potential.

title: Water transportation workers
rationale: Water transportation workers operate vessels in variable maritime environments with physical tasks like mooring and cargo handling. Autonomous vessels are in early trials but the unpredictable marine environment limits 2028 deployment.

title: Web developers and digital designers
rationale: Web developers create websites. Entirely desk-based knowledge work.

title: Welders, cutters, solderers, and brazers
rationale: Welding in manufacturing settings is highly structured and repetitive. Robotic welding is already widespread in automotive; by 2028 humanoid robots extend this to more welding tasks in controlled factory environments.

title: Wholesale and manufacturing sales representatives
rationale: Wholesale sales is primarily relationship-based selling and negotiation. This is knowledge and interpersonal work with no physical labor component for robots to automate.

title: Wind turbine technicians
rationale: Wind turbine technicians perform maintenance and repair at extreme heights in exposed, variable conditions. The hazardous and unpredictable work environment makes robotic replacement infeasible by 2028.

title: Woodworkers
rationale: Woodworking in factory settings involves operating machines and handling materials in semi-structured environments. CNC automation handles much cutting, but assembly and finishing still require human dexterity for varied products.

title: Writers and authors
rationale: Writers create written content. Entirely desk-based creative knowledge work.

title: Zoologists and wildlife biologists
rationale: Zoologists study animal behavior. Knowledge-based scientific work with some fieldwork.
